selection_assignments.rationale: Frontier Models anchor: MiniMax M3 is a major June open-weight model release combining sparse attention, long-context positioning, multimodal input and desktop-operation claims.
Frontier Models anchor: Anthropic's June 30 releases combine Claude Sonnet 5, Claude Science and a safety-framework update into a major end-of-month model and product transition.

AI for Science anchor: the near-autonomous chemistry workflow gives the June Special a distinctive real-world long-horizon scientific-agent case while preserving the explicit human-in-the-loop boundary.
Frontier Models section core: Alibaba's June lifecycle records Qwen3.7 updates plus later multimodal releases and regional model availability.
Frontier Models section core: Gemini API lifecycle changes show model preview/GA, computer-use, streaming speech and deprecation activity within the same month.
Frontier/Agents section core: Goal mode, /swarm and Kimi K2.7 Code connect model release activity directly to autonomous and multi-agent coding workflows.
Agents section core: SwarmX treats agentic workloads as schedulable multi-call/tool systems rather than isolated model requests.
Agents & Memory section core: ChatGPT Dreaming provides a deployed memory-architecture change and a concrete bridge from model capability to persistent user context.
Inference/Serving section core: Jalapeño adds the hardware layer to the month's serving story, while final performance remains explicitly preliminary.
Inference/Serving section core: FlashInfer v0.6.13 captures material Blackwell/GQA, attention/MoE, quantization and autotuning work in the kernel layer.
Inference/Serving section core: SGLang v0.5.14 links new-model support with serving and kernel changes across emerging frontier families.
Inference/Serving section core: vLLM v0.24.0 combines MiniMax-M3 support with Model Runner V2, diffusion and expert-parallel serving work.
Agent Safety/Security core: the paper makes the important systems distinction that capability exposure is not equivalent to per-call authorization.
Agent Safety/Security core: adaptive defense-aware prompt-injection evaluation provides a strong methodological axis beyond fixed attack suites.
Agent Safety/Security core: SafeClawArena frames persistent agents as computer systems and provides a broad cross-component adversarial evaluation surface.
Use the GPT-5.6 limited preview as a chronology bridge into the July family launch rather than duplicating July's FEATURE_CORE treatment.
Use Google DeepMind's June model and agent-safety chronology as supporting ecosystem context without creating another broad vendor article.
Use SmoothAgent as systems evidence for long-horizon agent serving and context transformation rather than as a separate article package.
Use Moebius to explain runtime MoE parallelism switching as a research complement to production serving-stack releases.
Use HMA-Serve to broaden the inference discussion toward memory-heterogeneous and disaggregated serving without turning author-reported gains into a standalone performance story.
Use ShareLock as a concrete MCP multi-tool poisoning example beneath the broader authorization and prompt-injection security themes.
Use Deployment Simulation as an operational safety-method complement to adversarial research, keeping OpenAI's reported effectiveness attribution explicit.
Use GPT-Rosalind as background for the AI-for-Science package, complementing the chemistry workflow without spending a second standalone science feature.
Retain the execution-time safety-kernel design as a concise research watch item; prototype/formal evidence is notable but not production validation.
Retain context-rot and premature-termination findings as a concise long-horizon research watch rather than expanding the Agents package further.
Retain MemDelta as a methodology watch on hidden confounds in agent-memory evaluation, with author-controlled evaluation boundaries intact.

Keep Daybreak/Codex Security/GPT-5.5-Cyber outside the main issue because access remains limited and the Security package is already dense; this is an editorial cut, not an Evidence-quality rejection.

Keep GLM-5.2 outside the main issue to avoid overloading the Frontier Models section after MiniMax, Anthropic, Alibaba, Gemini and Kimi coverage; this is editorial prioritization rather than a quality rejection.

architecture_proposal.editorial_thesis: 2026年6月は、生成AIのエージェント化がモデル単体の能力競争から、記憶・スケジューリング・推論基盤・権限境界・実世界の科学ワークフローまで実行系全体へ広がった月だった。
architecture_goals: 7月Specialと同じく、Evidenceを個別ニュースの羅列にせず6テーマのpackageへ統合し、主要記事材料を15件程度の粒度に保つ。
Frontier Modelsでは6月の主要リリースを比較しつつ、GPT-5.6 limited previewは7月の本格展開へつながるchronology bridgeとして扱い重複を抑える。
Agents & Memory、Inference & Serving、Agent Safety & Securityを別テーマとして扱い、長時間エージェント化がruntime・memory・authorizationへ波及した構造を示す。
AI for Scienceはnear-autonomous chemistry workflowを独立Featureとして扱い、完全自律ではないhuman-in-the-loop境界を明示する。
Issue #9に従い、published proseからCandidate Selection、Evidence Task、Reaction Pass等のpipeline jargonと制作TODOを排除し、why this Specialをreader-facingに示す。
Issue #40に従い、Technical Notesをreader-facing technical appendixとして設計し、完全Evidence IDやselection stateはRepository provenanceへ寄せる。
Theme Synthesis / Claim Boundary / Technical Notes境界は連続した誌面flowを前提とし、後段Visual Reviewで孤立box・blank page・大空白を全ページ検査する。
36ページを計画値とし、40ページを超える見込みならDraftへ進まずCandidate SelectionまたはArchitectureへ戻る。
